title: CLO Tips Classroom - Creating Custom Accessories
description:

chunks.title: CLO Tips Classroom - Creating Custom Accessories
chunks.content: ## Overview of Custom Component Creation in CLO This section explains the process of creating custom components (also called trims or accessories) in CLO, including using the Connect Mall for pre-made materials, designing components with shape panels, and converting them into usable trims. Important terms include "shape panel tool," "Connect Mall," "copy," and "trim format." --- ## Accessing and Using Components from the Connect Mall CLO provides a Connect Mall (accessible at connectclawset.com or via the CLO interface) where users can find and download various clothing materials and trims, including collaborations like SAB YKK. Components available here may have official copies (watermarked) that can be downloaded and used directly. - To access: Click the "N" icon in CLO, then Login. - Navigate to "Trim" materials to browse available components. - Some copies are complex and cannot be made with panels, but many can be created using shape panels, which will be demonstrated next. --- ## Creating Copies Using Shape Panels in CLO This section details how to create a custom trim component by drawing panels and converting them into a copy (component) in CLO. ### Step-by-Step Procedure: 1. **Prepare the Reference:** - Open the material document folder in the CLO library. - Use the shape panel tool in the 2D window to create a panel (default size: 500x500 mm). - Import a reference image by right-clicking in the picture shop window and adding it as a sticker. - Adjust the sticker's opacity to around 40-50% for better tracing. 2. **Draw Panels:** - The target copy consists of seven small panels; only three unique panels need to be drawn because some repeat. - Use the internal shape tool to draw: - Mouth-shaped panel - Curved panel - T-shaped panel (use the internal multi-demand shape tool, holding Shift to keep lines horizontal and vertical). 3. **Convert Lines to Boards:** - Use the adjustment board tool to convert internal lines to boards. - Right-click lines to select "Column" as the board. - For the T-shape, cut off unnecessary parts but keep internal lines for reference. - For the mouth shape, select the external line and cut it off to retain the internal line. 4. **Combine and Duplicate Boards:** - Arrange the boards properly by combining them. - Duplicate boards using Ctrl-D or Ctrl-C/V. - Rotate and align duplicates to form the full component shape. - Delete the original large panel once all smaller panels are duplicated and aligned. 5. **Rearrange and Adjust Boards:** - Select all boards, right-click in the 3D window, and choose "Rearrange 2D Arrangement Position" to sync 2D and 3D layouts. - Modify material and color in the 3D window (e.g., apply a golden metal effect). - Adjust thickness: 8 mm for mouth-shaped and T-shaped panels (thicker), 5 mm for middle panels (thinner). - Adjust edge curves and move boards slightly to create depth. 6.

Modify material and color in the 3D window (e.g., apply a golden metal effect). - Adjust thickness: 8 mm for mouth-shaped and T-shaped panels (thicker), 5 mm for middle panels (thinner). - Adjust edge curves and move boards slightly to create depth. 6. **Convert Boards into a Copy:** - Select all boards, right-click in 3D window, select "Convert" > "Copy." - The boards disappear in 2D and appear as a "copy" with a butterfly icon in 3D. - Adjust weight (e.g., 2 grams) and size using the copy icon. - Save the copy in trim format for reuse. --- ## Applying the Created Trim Component to Garments - Open a CLO project with a base garment (e.g., default t-shirt). - Find the saved trim format component in the library. - Right-click and add it to the workspace. - Use the glue tool to attach the trim to the garment. - The component is now usable as a custom accessory. --- ## Creating Components with Stickers or Textures This section covers making components that include stickers or textures, such as text or images, especially when the material has surface roughness or metallic maps. ### Important Considerations: - Simple conversion (right-click > convert) loses texture maps like roughness or metal maps. - A specialized workflow is needed to preserve these textures. ### Procedure: 1. **Open a New Project with the Metal Plate Texture File:** - This file includes textures such as displacement, surface roughness, and metal maps. 2. **Enter UV Editing Mode:** - Select the texture panel. - Click "Auto UV Fill" to map textures fully. 3. **Export Panels as OBJ:** - Return to simulation mode. - Select all panels and textures. - Export as OBJ with scale in millimeters (100%). - Enable saving textures as a ZIP file. 4. **Import and Add Attachment:** - Open a new CLO project. - Import the saved ZIP file as an "Attachment" object. - Set scale to millimeters (100%). 5. **Manually Reapply Missing Maps:** - In the property editor, displacement map and surface roughness map may be missing. - Open the material folder with the original maps. - Add displacement map and adjust particle spacing and displacement amount. - Add surface roughness map, set as texture, adjust data, and check "invert" if needed. - Increase metallic level to restore metal effects. 6. **Adjust Weight and Size:** - Select the attachment. - Set weight (e.g., 5 grams) and scale (e.g., 50 for smaller size). 7. **Save the Component:** - Save the trim format with all textures preserved. --- ## Applying Textured Components to Garments - After import and manual texture adjustments, the textured component can be added to garments using the glue tool.
